title: A Postcard for the Orchard
premise: Astrid Okafor's vineyard survives on a government preservation grant that requires her to host an anonymous pen-pal program meant to reconcile feuding families in her valley — and the letters pair her with Elias Brandt, heir to the bank foreclosing on her orchard. Their correspondence, written without names, turns tender before they discover each other's identities at the harvest festival, forcing Astrid to choose between exposing the grant fraud that could save her land and protecting Elias from his father's crimes. When Elias testifies against his family to save both the vineyard and her trust, Astrid learns that loyalty to truth is the only love that lasts; the book ends with them planting new vines together as the last train of the season leaves without either of them needing to be on it.
about_author: Petra Crane is a former agricultural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters in rural county offices before turning to fiction. She writes romances about people whose lives are measured in harvests, debts, and the courage to stay.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Seven years after inheriting her uncle's mortgaged vineyard, Astrid counts what remains: forty acres, one working press, and a preservation grant with strings attached — including mandatory participation in the valley's reconciliation pen-pal program. She writes her first guarded letter to 'a stranger.' Emotional beat: weary resilience masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias Brandt, sent home to process foreclosures for his father's bank, is ordered by the grant committee to join the same pen-pal program as reputation repair. He writes honestly for the first time in years, not knowing his correspondent owns the orchard he's been sent to take. Emotional beat: guilt he can't name.

chapters.title: Letters in the Press House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over weeks, the anonymous letters deepen — Astrid confesses her fear of failing her uncle's memory; Elias admits he hates his work. They begin noticing coincidences: shared weather, the same church bells. Neither suspects yet. Emotional beat: intimacy growing inside anonymity.

chapters.title: The Foreclosure Notice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A foreclosure notice arrives with a 60-day deadline, signed by E. Brandt. Astrid realizes her pen pal may be her enemy and stops writing — but finds she can't stop reading his latest letter, which describes wanting to 'burn the whole bank down from inside.' Emotional beat: betrayal colliding with reluctant hope.

chapters.title: What Elias Found in the Files
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Auditing old loans, Elias discovers his father falsified documents to strip the Okafor vineyard years ago — the debt Astrid inherited was manufactured. He begins quietly copying evidence, torn between family loyalty and the woman he's falling for through paper. Emotional beat: the first crack in duty.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the festival, a letter detail — a scarred left hand, a quoted poem — reveals their identities publicly. Astrid slaps him; Elias lets her. The crowd watches the bank's heir and the debtor's niece. Emotional beat: humiliation, fury, and underneath it, recognition.

chapters.title: The Grant Committee's Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The committee chair offers Astrid a deal: testify that the Brandt fraud never happened, keep her grant, and the valley's funding stays intact — or lose everything by telling the truth. She has until the last train of the season, three weeks. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Let Someone Stay After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts his father, who threatens to destroy Astrid entirely if Elias testifies. That night Elias appears at the vineyard gate after the last train has gone, asking to stay — not as a banker, but as the man from the letters. Astrid must decide whether to let him in. Emotional beat: vulnerability as surrender.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: at the hearing, Elias presents the forged documents despite his father's threats; Astrid refuses the committee's silence deal, risking the vineyard to back him. His father is exposed; the grant is frozen pending review; the foreclosure collapses. Both stand exposed and ruined-looking — and free. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: New Vines
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue-adjacent. Spring: the grant is restored under honest administration, the manufactured debt erased. Elias, disowned and lighter, plants vines beside her in the cold morning. The season's first train passes without either of them watching it go. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy — love that survived the truth.
